title: Ep 003 – Martin Scholz
guest_bio: B2B SaaS partnerships advisor based in Berlin; founder of CEG (capital-efficient growth). Former exec at Searchmetrics and Uberall who traded the executive travel grind for an advisory practice helping companies make partnerships work.
summary: Berlin advisor Martin Scholz on partnerships as the evolution of go-to-market: why 80% fail, what actually makes them work, and his reinvention from burnout-travel executive to a life that fits.

pull_quotes.text: I got the highest frequent-flyer tier and thought 'yes' — then realized it just means I'm away from my family too often.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: My wife said one sentence: 'I didn't marry jet lag.'

pull_quotes.text: You know what your superpower is? You're pretty good at reinventing yourself.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: 70 to 80% of partnerships in B2B SaaS fail. My vision is to bring that number down to 70.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: Partnerships work when they're understood as an evolution of your existing go-to-market.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: Nobody closes better than partner-sourced leads.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: Sales is transactional. Partnership is 'marry for 25 years' — you have to find the perfect fit.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: It's more critical to understand what's in it for them than what's in it for you.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: There's a difference between knowing something and really making it your own.

pull_quotes.speaker: Martin Scholz
pull_quotes.text: We accepted a dip in income for more flexibility and a lifetime.
